summary.headline: Chalet Q2 FY27 core revenue rose 11% YoY to INR 5,110 million and EBITDA 13% to INR 2,274 million, with margin up 110 bps to 45%.
summary.overview: Core business (Hospitality and CRE, excluding residential) grew revenue 11% YoY to INR 5,110 million, with EBITDA up 13% to INR 2,274 million and margin expanding 110 bps to 45%. Hospitality RevPAR rose 7.2% on 11.3% ADR growth, while resorts grew RevPAR 34% and MMR business hotels lagged due to Powai construction and weaker foreign travel. Management flagged that consolidated YoY comparisons are distorted by the Phase-I Koramangala residential handover in Q2 FY26, with Phase-II handovers (168 units, RERA date December 2026) to be booked in Q3 FY27. Credit rating was upgraded to IND AA by India Ratings, and planned capex for FY27-FY29 was raised to INR 34-36 billion after adding two ATHIVA properties; Taj Delhi airport timing may slip on GRAP restrictions.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: RevPAR +7.2% YoY on ADR +11.3%; room revenue +9.7%, F&B +6.4%. Blended resort occupancy 41.2% vs 32.6%; resort RevPAR +34%, with Westin Himalayas growing upward of 50-55%. MMR was subdued by Powai construction and weak international travel.

segments.name: Commercial Real Estate
segments.commentary: Monthly rental exit run-rate INR 300 million in September 2026 vs INR 290 million in June; occupancy about 91%, rising to 95% on available leasable area after a Bangalore LOI. Guidance of INR 320 million monthly by March 2027.

guidance_outlook: CIGNUS 2 Powai (about 1 million sq ft leasable) on track for substantial completion by FY27 end; expected to start contributing in FY28.
Taj at Delhi International Airport (380 keys) inventory launch now pointed to FY28; 70 rooms earlier guided for the last quarter of FY27 may slip into Q1 FY28 due to GRAP restrictions.
Management said the two large projects should add a minimum of double-digit revenue growth to FY28, excluding geopolitical impacts.

Planned capex of INR 34-36 billion over FY27-FY29, raised from about INR 30 billion because of two ATHIVA properties (Hyderabad and Pune); no cost overruns reported, to be largely funded by internal accruals.
Target portfolio of 5,500 keys and beyond within five years (75-80% capacity addition); pipeline 2,036 keys.
CRE monthly rentals expected to reach INR 320 million by March 2027; full CRE portfolio around INR 500 crore annual rentals once CIGNUS 2 is leased.
Varca (Goa) construction expected to start in Q4 FY27 after CRZ and MoEF approvals.
Koramangala commercial space (about 160,000 sq ft) targeted for completion by FY28, possibly to a single tenant.
capex_capacity: Taj Delhi airport: 380 keys; launch of inventory in early FY28; GRAP restrictions in NCR being monitored.
CIGNUS 2 Powai: about 1 million sq ft leasable; substantial completion targeted by FY27 end.
ATHIVA: about 900 keys in pipeline across five properties in four locations; portfolio to reach 1,200 keys; Khandala and Navi Mumbai operational.

ATHIVA Pulse Navi Mumbai (ex-Four Points by Sheraton) relaunched as Autograph Collection after about INR 1 billion investment (management also cited INR 100 crore); The Daily Club wellness floor of 30,000 sq ft.
Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad and Hyatt Regency Airoli being developed by Mindspace; management says on schedule. Varca (Goa) construction delayed by approvals.
demand_pricing: Quarter saw YoY air traffic contraction in Mumbai, Bangalore and Hyderabad; Delhi grew, aided by BRICS summit and MICE demand.
Powai impacted by CIGNUS 2 construction; porch re-opened restoring banquet access; 20 rooms per day of Crew business signed back against about 100 lost.
Hyderabad saw strong RevPAR growth from GCC and corporate demand; Bangalore growth moderate as foreign-tourist dependent, with 130 additional rooms released during the Middle East crisis.
Management expects foreign travel to recover after the US midterm elections and easing West Asia disruption; Q3 business-on-books described as a clear positive; weddings strong in Q4.
Large MICE and group business grew only about 4% for Chalet, which management said was the reason F&B lagged room revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 revenue growth be significantly higher, around 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the analyst was 'not wrong', citing minimum double-digit revenue growth from CIGNUS 2 and Taj Delhi on top of existing portfolio growth, excluding geopolitical impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Varca and Airoli timelines change, and will Mindspace's building completion dates delay fit-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Varca slipped due to Goa CRZ and MoEF approvals; construction to start Q4 FY27. Fit-out runs parallel with building work, so the gap to opening is short; Airoli hotel only starts from the 25th-26th floor and is on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is Chalet's leverage outlook given higher capex and gross debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt has been stable at about INR 1,900-2,100 crore over the last three quarters; capex increase reflects two added ATHIVA assets, with no cost increases on any project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MMR occupancy stuck in the mid-60s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited weak international demand, Powai construction, a shift of air traffic to the new Navi Mumbai terminal, and a late-quarter lack of wedding dates; recovery expected in H2 with MICE and weddings returning.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected resort occupancy levels and initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 resort occupancy 46.1% and Q2 41.2%; management reiterated a 60-65% ideal target, expects a seasonal jump in H2, and says ATHIVA Khandala is in its first year with about 80% of fair share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope for CRE rental run-rate growth ex-CIGNUS 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate expected to reach about INR 320 million by March 2027 from the signed LOI and CIGNUS 1 talks; occupancy about 91% weighted average.

risks_watch: Taj Delhi airport launch may slip from Q4 FY27 into Q1 FY28 due to GRAP restrictions in NCR; monitor the revised date.
Varca (Goa) construction has not started after two years since acquisition; approvals pending at MoEF in Delhi.
MMR occupancy remains in mid-60s; recovery depends on international and MICE demand and Powai ramp-up.
Gross debt rose about INR 400 crore since March 2026; leverage to be watched against INR 34-36 billion capex plan.
Koramangala Phase-II handover and revenue recognition in Q3 FY27 (RERA date December 2026); FY28 Bangalore commercial tower completion.
Management declined to give exact quarters for FY29 deliveries (three properties, about 625 keys) beyond 'within the financial year'.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand recovery, resorts and CRE, with clear timeline guidance; more cautious and hedged on Taj Delhi timing, Varca and MMR occupancy, which management attributed to external factors and construction.
key_quotes: If I had to sum up this quarter in one word, it would be “Readiness”.
With these two significant projects coming online, it should contribute minimum double-digits to our revenue growth.
Now that it's two years since we acquired Varca and we have still not started pouring concrete is indeed disappointing, but it's not for lack of effort.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

tone.note: Management was confident on resort RevPAR (+34%), CRE rental growth and the FY28 double-digit growth outlook, but hedged on Taj Delhi timing (GRAP), Varca approvals and MMR occupancy in the mid-60s; analysts pushed on FY28 growth of around 20%, leverage given higher capex, and MMR weakness.
